name: Furniture/mattress returns resale rep (ShareTown model)
one_liner: Pick up like-new returned furniture and mattresses from online brands, then resell them locally on marketplaces and split the sale price with the platform.
customer: Local buyers on Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist and OfferUp; the online furniture/mattress brands supply the stock
offer: Like-new returned mattresses and furniture, listed with photos and descriptions the platform provides
how_it_makes_money: Revenue share: the rep splits the final sale price with ShareTown; mattresses sell for $300-$700
startup_cost: low-medium (needs a van or large vehicle and storage space at home; no amount stated)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (sign-up is a 'very simple and easy form to fill out online')
evidence: ShareTown hires reps in each town to collect returned furniture that can't fit back in the box (AJv_ZScvQdE)
You split the final sale price with ShareTown; mattresses sell for $300 to $700 (AJv_ZScvQdE)
Testimonials of people making $3,000-$4,000 a month (AJv_ZScvQdE)
risks: ShareTown is a US platform, and UK availability is unconfirmed
Needs physical handling, transport and storage
Income depends on how many returns come in locally
Evidence comes from platform testimonials, not verified figures

name: Local junk removal
one_liner: Haul away unwanted bulky items such as TVs and mattresses for a per-job fee.
customer: Households getting rid of bulky items
how_it_makes_money: Per-job fee, for example $60 to haul off a TV and a mattress
startup_cost: low-medium (needs a vehicle; disposal costs not stated)
evidence: '$60 to haul off a TV and a mattress' (AJv_ZScvQdE)
Mentioned as something to pair with ShareTown (AJv_ZScvQdE)
risks: Weak evidence: only a teaser clip is in the digest
In the UK a waste carrier licence is required and tip fees apply
Manual, in-person work that doesn't fit async-first goals

name: Retail arbitrage to Amazon (discount stores to FBA)
one_liner: Buy name-brand products cheaply at discount retailers and resell them on Amazon at a markup.
offer: Discounted name-brand products resold on Amazon
how_it_makes_money: Margin between the discount-store price and the Amazon sale price, minus Amazon fees
tools: TJ Maxx (TK Maxx in the UK)
evidence: 'I sold almost $5 million worth of name brand products on Amazon' (AJv_ZScvQdE)
'Going to TJ Maxx today to see what I can find to resell on Amazon' (AJv_ZScvQdE)
'One more sale will hit $50,000' (AJv_ZScvQdE; context unclear)
risks: Weak evidence: the $5M is gross sales from a featured creator, and no margins are given
Brand-gating and IP complaints on Amazon
Sourcing in store takes time and isn't async
